Illinois Brick Co. v. Illinois, 431 U.S. 720 (1977) — https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/431/720/
Reiter v. Sonotone Corp., 442 U.S. 330 (1979) — https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/442/330/
original_excerpt:
From Illinois Brick Co. v. Illinois, 431 U.S. 720, 728–729, 746 (1977):
The Court held that direct purchasers are the parties injured within the meaning of Clayton Act § 4 and barred the offensive use of pass-on theories, concluding that antitrust enforcement is better served by concentrating full overcharge recovery in direct purchasers rather than attempting to apportion damages among indirect purchasers in the distribution chain.

From Reiter v. Sonotone Corp., 442 U.S. 330, 334 n.2, 337 (1979):
The Court held that retail consumers paying higher prices for personal-use goods sustain an injury in their "property" under § 4, explicitly clarifying that its review was restricted to the consumer "property" statutory term and did not alter or disturb the direct-purchaser rule of Illinois Brick.
fidelity: Core indirect-purchaser/pass-on and consumer-property distinction is supported. Reiter leaves direct-purchaser issues outside review; it does not affirmatively adjudicate them.
scope_note: Federal §4 overcharge recovery, subject to the opinion's recognized exceptions; not all antitrust injury or state-law remedies.
